19         Defendants oppose Plaintiff’s motion for an award of service fees as follows:
20                                       INTRODUCTION
21         This is a frivolous case filed by designated vexatious litigant, Sergey Firsov (“Mr.
22   Firsov”), putatively on behalf of his 8 year-old son, L.F. 1 Plaintiff’s motion contains
23   material misrepresentations. Contrary to Mr. Firsov’s assertions, neither defendant was
24   lawfully served with the summons and complaint; no one “crumpled down docs and
25   through it to trash”; and most important, neither defendant was actually or “formally
26   served.” Indeed, the Motion for service fees itself was never served and no proof of
27
     1
28     Throughout papers submitted in the docket by Mr. Firsov, he provides the actual name of his
     son, despite Rule 5.2, F.R.C.P.


                     OPPOSITION TO MOTION SERVICE COSTS FEES - 25-CV-03265 SVK
            Case 5:25-cv-03265-SVK      Document 34     Filed 08/07/25    Page 2 of 11



 1   service is in the docket. To avoid Mr. Firsov’s further destruction of time of the Court
 2   and defendants, and notwithstanding these failures, the undersigned counsel has entered
 3   an appearance in this action and will timely file a responsive pleading.
 4         Plaintiff’s Motion for an award of service costs should be denied.
 5                                       Statement of Facts
 6         Sometime in 2023, Mr. Firsov sought to participate in religious services at
 7   defendant Church of Scientology Silicon Valley. In late 2024 he made a donation on line
 8   to a Church of Scientology in Florida. For reasons not addressed here, Mr. Firsov was
 9   informed that he would not be permitted to participate at that Church, and his donation
10   was returned. After it was learned that Mr. Firsov was dismissed from the organized
11   Church generally, Defendants informed him that he and his family were no longer
12   welcome at either of the defendant Churches in this District where he lives.
13         The gist of the Complaint is that Mr. Firsov alleges that his 8-year-old son was
14   discriminated against because his father was dismissed from the religion. He also makes
15   non sequitur allegations regarding refusal of the Churches to allow him to have a concert
16   in the Church. The Complaint alleges that such conduct constitutes discrimination in
17   violation of federal employment law – the only reference to any federal “right” therein.
18   Mr. Firsov seeks $345 and an order “banning” Scientology in the entire country because
19   the Churches “banned” his son from membership. None of these claims are justiciable,
20   and none present any federal claim to which relief could be granted.
21                                         Service Issues
22         The docket reveals Mr. Firsov submitted two Proofs of Service of the Complaint.
23   The first was by one “Pomohaibo Myron,” who “signed” the proof by writing the initials
24   “P.M.E.” and claimed to have “personally served the summons on the individual”:
25   Church of Scientology Silicon Valley, on July 18, 2025. (Docket # 32.) This is not
26   accurate. “Personal service” of a corporation in California is effectuated generally by
27   service of the designated registered agent for service of process, or of a corporate officer
28   or general manager pursuant to §416.10, Cal. Code. Civ. Pro.
                                                  2
                     OPPOSITION TO MOTION FOR SERVICE COSTS - 25-CV-03265 SVK
            Case 5:25-cv-03265-SVK       Document 34     Filed 08/07/25    Page 3 of 11



 1         In this incident, a process server walked into Church reception on the evening of
 2   July 18, 2025, and went to the reception desk where a Church staff member was seated.
 3   The man said he had an item, some papers, he needed to give to someone. He was
 4   informed by the receptionist that he could not accept the papers. The process server did
 5   not ask for the registered agent, nor someone in charge or an officer, director or
 6   executive. Rather, the man stated only that he needed to give “it” to someone. The
 7   receptionist stated he was sorry, but he could not take the papers. The process server
 8   then departed the building. He came back a few minutes later, placed the papers on the
 9   desk and walked out, saying “I’m just leaving it here.” The man then left the building
10   and did not return. (Ex. A. Declaration of Samuel Stokes.) The sworn assertion on the
11   proof states, “Defendant’s staff were mad, clumbled [sic] documents and through[sic] in
12   trash” is a falsehood. Nothing remotely like that occurred. (Stokes Declaration.) Indeed,
13   no person with the name Pomohaibo Myron could be located in a public records check
14   in California, much less as a service professional, and the initials “P.M.E.” affixed to the
15   sworn proof, suggest someone of a different name signed the paper. This was not lawful
16   service, much less professional service for which Mr. Firsov would have paid $150.
17         Mr. Firsov signed the other proof of service on “the individual” of Church of
18   Scientology Mission of Silicon Valley, allegedly at Pedro Street in San Jose. (Docket #
19   32.) It contains the identical false assertion that appears in the Pomohaibo Myron Proof,
20   written in the same broken English: “Defendant’s staff were mad, clumbled documents
21   and through it to trash.” [sic] However, Mr. Firsov is not qualified to effectuate service,
22   as the papers filed in the action identify Plaintiff as “L.F., minor, by and through his
23   parent and guardian ad litem Sergey Firsov.” Service by a party is prohibited by
24   §414.10, Cal. Code of Civ. Pro. applicable to federal service in this District. While there
25   was also no lawful service procedurally, we shall spare the details thereof, as Mr. Firsov
26   is legally incapable, as the de facto, if not the de jure plaintiff, to serve the summons.
27   //
28   //
                                                   3
                      OPPOSITION TO MOTION FOR SERVICE COSTS - 25-CV-03265 SVK
            Case 5:25-cv-03265-SVK      Document 34     Filed 08/07/25   Page 4 of 11



 1                                        CONCLUSION
 2         The undersigned has voluntarily appeared on behalf of the Defendants in this case,
 3   so no motion to quash service has or will be filed.
 4         But the Plaintiff’s motion to be awarded formal service fees for himself and a
 5   neighbor (the Pomohaibo Myron proof contains the same address), makes material
 6   misrepresentations. There was no lawful personal service. Mr. Firsov is a genuine
 7   vexatious litigant (Exhibit B, Vexatious litigant order), having filed 38 lawsuits in the
 8   Santa Clara Superior Court alone, and another 14 lawsuits in this Court. He continues to
 9   pump out vexatious litigation. A cursory review of the largely incomprehensible and
10   non-justiciable Complaint in this action manifests a continuing vexatious streak.
11         Defendants respectfully request that Mr. Firsov’s motion for an award of service
12   costs, be denied.
13   Dated: August 6, 2025                         Respectfully submitted,
